specAnchors.text: describe energy transfers involving energy stores: • energy stores: chemical, kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, magnetic, electrostatic, nuclear • energy transfers: mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation (light and sound)

primer.text: Every energy argument in this course runs on one model: eight stores that hold energy and four pathways that move it. This note fixes the vocabulary — system, equilibrium, stores, pathways — so that later calculations always have somewhere precise to put the joules.

modules.title: Systems and energy stores
modules.opening: Physics borrows a bookkeeping idea to keep energy arguments tidy: define a system — an object or group of objects — and then only energy crossing its boundary matters. Inside the accounts, eight named stores hold the energy while anything changing moves it between them.
keyPoints: A system means an object or a group of objects chosen for study.
Defining the system narrows the physics to what is relevant for the situation being observed.
A system in equilibrium transfers nothing; any change to the system moves energy between stores.
There are eight energy stores: kinetic, gravitational, elastic, magnetic, electrostatic, chemical, nuclear and thermal.
Moving objects fill the kinetic store; lifted objects fill the gravitational store; hotter objects fill the thermal store.

low.restatement: A system is any object or group of objects; changes to it transfer energy between the eight named stores, and an unchanged system in equilibrium transfers nothing.
low.analogy: A ledger with eight named accounts: nothing is spent or created, money simply moves between accounts whenever something happens to the system.
low.examPointer: Learn the eight stores as a fixed list — classification questions expect the exact names, not paraphrases.

medium.restatement: The system boundary decides which energy transfers are counted: an apple on a table transfers energy only once the table is removed, and the accounting then runs from the gravitational store into the kinetic store as it falls.
medium.analogy: Choosing a fence around a farm: only animals crossing the fence are counted, and the fence you draw changes the whole story.
medium.examPointer: State the system explicitly in long answers: the same falling apple is a different story if the Earth is inside or outside the system.

modules.title: Energy transfer pathways
modules.opening: Stores hold energy; pathways move it. The model names exactly four: mechanical work, electrical work, heating and radiation (light and sound). Any everyday transfer you can describe — a kettle, a falling apple, sunlight on a wall — reduces to these four crossings between stores.
keyPoints: Energy is transferred between stores by four pathways: mechanically, electrically, by heating and by radiation.
Mechanical work involves a force acting through a distance.
Electrical work transfers energy through moving charge in a circuit.
Heating covers particle-to-particle transfer such as conduction, and radiation (light and sound) transfers energy without a material medium.

low.restatement: Four pathways carry energy between the eight stores: mechanical, electrical, heating, and radiation (light and sound); every device description is a pathway joining two stores.
low.analogy: Four roads between eight towns: the stores are the towns and every journey of energy takes one of the four roads.
low.examPointer: When a question says describe the transfer, name BOTH the stores and the pathway: store → pathway → store.

medium.restatement: The pathway table separates how the energy crosses the boundary: force-through-distance is mechanical, charge-in-a-circuit is electrical, particle collisions are heating, and waves leaving the object are radiation.
medium.analogy: Payment methods for the same money: cash, card, transfer and bitcoin all move the same pounds between the same accounts.
medium.examPointer: Light and sound both count as radiation pathways — exam answers often forget sound is included.

glossary.definition: An object or group of objects chosen as the focus of an energy description.
The state of a system in which nothing changes, so no energy is transferred.
One of the eight named places energy can be held: kinetic, gravitational, elastic, magnetic, electrostatic, chemical, nuclear or thermal.
One of the four ways energy moves between stores: mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation.
